en.title: Minimum Car Removals for a Two-Car Bridge
en.description:
Cars enter the bridge in their original order; when one leaves, the next enters, so at most two adjacent cars are on the bridge at a time. Cars may be removed in advance, and the remaining cars keep their relative order. Find the minimum number of removals so that the total weight never exceeds the capacity. A single car may not exceed the capacity either.

This site uses a standard input/output protocol; ranges not given by the source are stated explicitly.
en.input: The first line contains N capacity, and the second line contains N weights. N is 1..100000 and the weights are 1..10⁹; the source gives no bound on the capacity, and this site uses 1..2×10⁹.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: Example 1: every adjacent sum is ≤8, so remove 0. Example 2: after removing 7, the cars 3, 2, 6, 1 are all compatible, so remove 1. Example 3: 9 alone exceeds the capacity; after removing it, 2+2 is exactly 4, so remove 1.
hints: Scan while keeping track of the current last kept car. A car that overloads on its own is removed directly; if it overloads together with the last car, one of the two must be removed, so keep the lighter one; otherwise append it.
